analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia
key_insights: US equities fell on Wednesday: S&P 500 -1.11% (close 7718.94), Nasdaq -1.88%, Dow -0.09%. The S&P 500 broke a 53-session streak without a 1%+ daily decline, the longest since a 74-day streak into early 2020.

AI trade came under pressure. The SOX was down 10% over six sessions and is on track for its longest losing streak since May 2025. MU fell in eight of the last nine sessions. Neocloud debt and funding came under scrutiny, led by CRWV.

September core CPI was hotter than expected: core +0.3% m/m vs 0.2% consensus, annual core 2.6%, headline +0.6% m/m. Supercore (ex-energy and housing) was the hottest since January. BofA kept its October hike call and Citi moved to a December hike.

Fed hike odds swung during the day. October hike odds were near 60% from about 20% before the release per one section, and 32% (down from above 50%) per the recap. Hikes priced through year-end fell to 30 bp from above 35 bp. The 2Y yield fell more than 15 bp from its morning peak.

Banks lagged after Q3 results. BAC earnings were light excluding a $1.2B regulatory charge, with FICC down 17% y/y. MS beat, with record Wealth Management revenue of $9.07B, but equity underwriting and FICC were weak. STT fee income was soft.

Barclays downgraded NTAP, HPE and DELL to equal weight from overweight on valuation, with shares up roughly 125%, 185% and 350% YTD. DELL was also cited for decelerating AI server growth. The stocks fell 7.0%, 8.2% and 11.4%.

Oil rose 1.0% on Middle East escalation. A Houthi missile strike damaged Saudi Aramco's Dhahran headquarters, and Iranian officials threatened a full Strait of Hormuz closure. The IEA sees diesel prices staying elevated into 2027.

ASML raised FY26 sales guidance to EUR44-45B from EUR43-45B and said capacity additions will fall short of 2027-28 demand. Q4 guidance was slightly soft, and ASML-US fell 3.9% despite the beat and raise.

ECB President Lagarde said France's borrowing costs must be solved by Paris, not ECB intervention. French 10-year yields eased from early-October highs near 4.9%, the highest since 2002. OAT-Bund spreads peaked above 140 bp, widest since late 2011.
BoE chief economist Pill questioned market pricing of four 25 bp hikes over the next year. Gilt 10-year yields fell 2.6 bp to 5.428% and UK housebuilders and property stocks rallied.

China September exports rose 36.3% y/y to $447.2B versus 25.5% consensus, with a trade surplus of $133.5B. Integrated circuit exports were nearly $45B, up 136% in value. PPI rose to 5.0% y/y versus 4.4% consensus, and CPI was 0.9% versus 1.0% consensus.
MAS held Singapore policy unchanged against expectations of slight tightening. Q3 GDP grew 5.4% y/y versus 5.0% consensus.
Bloomberg sources say BOJ officials lean against a back-to-back hike in October but may hike in December. OIS prices about 10% for October and 88% for December.
BofA Asia FMS: 70% see AI monetization as the primary APAC equity driver over the next year. Taiwan is seen as the biggest AI beneficiary, and APAC inflation expectations jumped 25 ppt to 50%.
Precious metals sold off. Gold fell 1.33% to 4105.37 and silver fell 6.1%, its worst day since June. The dollar index rose 0.4%.

Upcoming US data: Thursday brings PPI, retail sales, jobless claims, Empire and Philly Fed. Fed's Hammack and Chair Warsh speak after Thursday's close. Import prices and industrial production follow on Friday.

market_movers.rationale: Barclays cut to equal weight from overweight on valuation after shares rose about 125% YTD. Stock fell 7.0%.
Barclays cut to equal weight from overweight on valuation after shares rose about 185% YTD. Stock fell 8.2%.
Barclays cut to equal weight from overweight, citing decelerating growth in AI servers and shares up about 350% YTD. Stock fell 11.4%.
Jefferies downgraded Swiss Re to underperform on accelerating reinsurance price declines and revenue risk, and cut its FY2027 revenue forecast by 12%.
Peel Hunt cut Admiral's target to 2,460p from 2,620p, expecting policy-volume gains to erode as UK motor rates rise.
Berenberg initiated Carmila at buy, citing earnings resilience, tenant diversification and a 12.5% FY2027 earnings yield.
2032 unsecured debt yields above 15%. DA Davidson's Luria warned the stock could go to zero if the company cannot repay its debt. Stock fell 15.5%.

earnings_insights: BAC Q3: earnings light excluding a $1.2B government fine (reported), with fee income and FICC/equities trading below the Street. FICC revenue fell 17% y/y.

MS Q3: earnings and revenue reported better than expected. Wealth Management revenue was a record $9.07B with $232B in net new assets. Equities revenue was $5.80B (+41% y/y), FICC was $2.01B, and equity underwriting was below consensus.
BLK Q3: reported margin expansion and strong long-term inflows.

STT Q3: reported earnings and revenue largely in line. NII was above consensus, fee income was light, and the FY26 fee revenue midpoint is a shade below the Street. FY expense-growth guidance was raised.
FAST Q3 reported largely in line, with September average daily sales softer than expected.
AZZ reported a beat and raise, with organic sales growth.

ASML Q3 reported revenue was EUR11.7B, in line, with stronger-than-expected profitability and EPS. FY26 sales guidance was raised to EUR44-45B and gross margin set at 56%. Q4 guidance was slightly soft.
LQDA: preliminary 3Q Yutrepia sales up 31% q/q, ahead of consensus.
EVT-DE preliminary 9M revenue and adjusted EBITDA beat consensus. FY guidance is about EUR465M revenue and a EUR42.8M adjusted EBITDA loss, versus expected EUR429M and a EUR45M loss.
LONN-CH raised its mid-term EBITDA margin target to 37-39% from 32-34% at its CMD.
Robert Walters Q3 net fees were up 1% at constant currency after 13 consecutive quarters of decline.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Hotter than expected on core services and goods, raising Fed hike odds.
Fastest since February, driven by AI-related shipments.
Fuel prices drove the increase; food prices were the main drag.
Upstream prices and fuel drove the increase.
Growth slowed from 6.2% in Q2 but beat forecasts.
Market pricing fell back after the morning CPI reaction.
BOJ leans against an October move.

risk_factors: Hot core inflation could push the Fed to hike in October or December.
AI-complex debt and funding stress, especially neocloud credit such as CRWV 2032 debt above 15% yield.
Middle East escalation and a possible Strait of Hormuz closure threaten oil supply, with diesel an upside risk.
French fiscal problems and 2027 election risk keep OAT-Bund spreads wide.
UK Budget on 28-Oct could be judged on the credibility of its funding measures.
European gas storage is about 15% below the five-year average according to Eurointelligence, and Qatar is shipping under a quarter of pre-war LNG volumes.
Singapore MAS warned inflation could last into 2027.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility index at 16.87, up 10.48% on the day and up 13.68% for the week.
European Fund Manager Survey shows France as the least favoured EU position, with a record 56% underweight.
BofA Asia FMS: 45% are overweight with no hedging or rotating within AI, versus 25% in September. Rotation into defensives faded.
Gold fell 1.33% and silver 6.1%, its worst day since June.
geopolitical: A Houthi missile strike damaged Saudi Aramco's Dhahran headquarters. The Houthis claimed 42 strikes in 24 hours.
Iranian officials threatened a complete Strait of Hormuz closure and said Tehran is targeting vessels in the Strait and the Gulf of Oman.
Netanyahu said he is not in favor of striking Iran before Israeli elections on 27-Oct.
China and the EU agreed to cap imports of Chinese hybrid cars.
Press reports say the Trump administration may reconsider the permit for the Orsted Revolution Wind project.
cross_bank_references: BofA maintained its October hike call, while Citi shifted to a December hike.
Goldman Sachs called the European sell-off more structural and stayed neutral on French rates.
Bank of America upgraded French stocks to overweight, while the European Fund Manager Survey showed France as the least favoured position.
Citi base case for Q4 TTF is EUR56/MWh versus the current level near EUR84.

tension_points.bull_case: ASML sees demand outstripping supply through 2028, with orders already placed for 2028. BofA Asia FMS shows 45% overweight or rotating within AI and fewer respondents see AI as fully priced in.
tension_points.bear_case: Neocloud debt scrutiny (CRWV 2032 debt above 15% yield), Barclays valuation downgrades of NTAP, HPE and DELL, and a 10% SOX decline over six sessions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further widening of neocloud debt yields or further sell-side downgrades on valuation would undermine the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: Bowman sees no urgency to hike again, and Goolsbee stressed the trend matters. Hike odds fell to 32% for October by the close.
tension_points.bear_case: Hot core CPI with supercore the highest since January. BofA kept its October hike call and Citi moved to a December hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Thursday's PPI and retail sales, and Chair Warsh's remarks Thursday night.

tension_points.bull_case: BofA upgraded French stocks to overweight at a 5% P/E discount, the widest since 2016.
tension_points.bear_case: Lagarde ruled out ECB intervention, French fiscal and 2027 election risks persist, and the Fund Manager Survey shows a record 56% underweight.
